How we work

We want advanced AI work to feel concrete, not vague.

NTS runs on a simple loop: compress wisely, adapt thoughtfully, evaluate honestly, ship usefully, and then do it again. The goal is not spectacle. The goal is sharp engineering with student energy.

Motto: Build light. Think deeply. Ship what matters.

Main lanes

Four practical directions for the first chapter.

Lane 01

Efficient language systems

Low-bit LLMs, quantization choices, memory tradeoffs, and realistic model behavior.

Lane 02

UTN student assistant

A focused chatbot for future UTN students, treated as both a useful product and an engineering test bed.

Lane 03

Alignment and evaluation

Usefulness, grounding, trust, and what a good student-facing system should actually feel like.

Lane 04

Future labs

Once the foundation is strong, the group expands into VLMs, world models, and member-led experiments.

Group rhythm

We learn by moving in public.

Build nights

Short sessions for prototypes, debugging, and visible progress.

Workshops

Focused walkthroughs that turn complex ideas into repeatable practice.

Reading and critique

Papers matter, but only if they sharpen what we build next.

Ready to build

NTS is for UTN students who want less hype and more real work.

Organizers: Sagnik Das and Vaibhav Prajapati. Contact: contact@agentlane.me.
